You are the implementing engineer for Atlas ERP, in '/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp' on branch feat/onboarding (dev merged; industry template layer 14.1 done). NO git commands. uv at ~/.local/bin/uv; run `cd backend && ~/.local/bin/uv run <cmd>`. PostgreSQL 16 at postgresql+asyncpg://atlas:atlas@localhost:55432/atlas (LOCAL — run the full pg suite).

This builds the TENANT ONBOARDING WIZARD: company info → pick industry template → COA/units/tax/workflows/numbering instantiated automatically (it ties together tenant creation + the 14.1 industry loader + the initial admin user/role).

READ FIRST (binding): the build spec ("Tenant onboarding wizard: company info → industry template → COA, units, tax codes, workflows, demo data instantiated automatically" / PLAN 14.2); docs/architecture.md D-060 (the 14.1 industry loader apply_template — onboarding CALLS it), D-007 (a NEW tenant is created under system_context — the four sanctioned system_context sites include tenant provisioning), D-008/D-009 (the onboarding creates the tenant's FIRST admin user + an admin role with the permission catalog — this bootstraps access; reuse admin/core auth+rbac), D-011 (run_in_uow), D-012/D-013/D-022/D-025. Then read the EXACT code:
- backend/app/modules/industry/loader.py + queries.py (apply_template(session, tenant_id, name) + list_templates — onboarding calls these) + the industry router (where apply currently lives).
- backend/app/modules/admin/ (Tenant + TenantSetting models + service — onboarding CREATES the Tenant; admin owns it) + admin/service.py (existing tenant/role helpers).
- backend/app/core/{tenancy.py (system_context — onboarding provisions under it), auth.py (password hashing — the first admin user needs a password; BUT per the safety rules, do NOT have the agent invent/handle real passwords improperly — the onboarding API takes an admin email + password for the new tenant's first user, hashed via the existing argon2 path; this is normal tenant signup, fine), rbac.py (the permission catalog + role creation — the admin role gets the full catalog or an admin permission set), numbering.py, deps.py, events.py}.
- How auth/login resolves a tenant (login takes tenant_slug + email + password) — the onboarding creates a tenant with a slug + an admin user who can then log in.
- backend/tests (admin/industry factories + the system_context test pattern).
Latest migration = 0043 (14.2 likely needs NO new tables — it orchestrates existing ones: Tenant, User, Role, + the industry apply; confirm and skip migration unless you add an onboarding-record table, which is optional — prefer recording onboarding status on the Tenant or via the existing industry config record).

§5 note: onboarding orchestrates tenant + admin-user + role creation (admin/core owned) + calls industry.loader.apply_template. Where does the onboarding ORCHESTRATOR live? It creates a Tenant (admin), a User + Role (core/admin), and applies an industry template (industry). This is a top-level provisioning flow. Put it in the ADMIN module (admin owns tenants + onboarding per PLAN 14) as `admin/service/onboarding.py` (or admin/onboarding.py) — admin may import core (auth/rbac/tenancy) and industry/loader? admin importing industry.loader is admin→industry; industry is newer and imports core+admin... wait, 14.1 said industry imports admin (for TenantSettings). So admin→industry AND industry→admin would be a CYCLE. AVOID: the onboarding orchestrator should NOT live in admin if admin can't import industry. RESOLUTION OPTIONS: (a) put onboarding in the INDUSTRY module (industry already imports admin, so industry/onboarding.py can create the tenant via admin's service + apply its own template — but creating a User/Role is core/admin). (b) put onboarding in a NEW thin top-level place. (c) Re-examine: does industry actually import admin/SERVICE, or admin MODELS? 14.1 said industry writes terminology/module-toggle TenantSettings — if it does that via an admin provisioning HANDLER (admin subscribes to IndustryTemplateApplying) rather than importing admin/service, then admin does NOT depend on industry and industry does NOT import admin/service → admin can import industry.loader cleanly, and onboarding lives in admin. CHECK what 14.1 actually did (read industry/loader.py — does it import admin.service or publish to an admin handler?). 
   - If industry/loader imports admin.service (admin→nothing, industry→admin): then admin importing industry.loader creates admin→industry→admin CYCLE. In that case put onboarding in industry OR make onboarding a core-level orchestrator. 
   - The CLEANEST: onboarding lives in the **industry** module (it already orchestrates provisioning + imports admin), OR in a dedicated path. DECIDE based on what 14.1 wired and document in D-061. Strong preference: keep it simple and §5-legal — read industry/loader.py first, then choose the module that already has the right import direction. If industry imports admin.service, put onboarding in industry/onboarding.py (industry→admin for tenant/user creation + industry's own apply). If 14.1 used an admin handler (no industry→admin/service import), put onboarding in admin/service/onboarding.py (admin→industry.loader). EITHER is fine — pick the legal one and document.

TASK — PLAN 14.2: tenant onboarding wizard. Build:

1. constants/permissions: an onboarding permission — but onboarding CREATES a tenant, which is a SYSTEM/superadmin action (not a tenant-scoped permission, since the tenant doesn't exist yet). The onboarding endpoint is either (a) unauthenticated public signup, or (b) a system/superadmin-guarded endpoint. For v1, model it as a system-level endpoint: POST /api/v1/onboarding/tenants is guarded by a system-admin check (a special permission or a system flag) OR documented as the public signup entrypoint. DECIDE: a simple system-admin-guarded onboarding endpoint (a platform operator creates tenants); document the auth model. (Avoid a fully-open public signup for v1 security; a system-admin or bootstrap-token guard is cleaner — document.)
2. The onboarding service `onboard_tenant(session, company_info, industry_template, admin_user)` under system_context + run_in_uow, idempotent (by tenant slug — re-onboarding an existing slug is a 409):
   - create the Tenant (slug from company name, name, etc.) via admin.
   - create the tenant's admin Role with the permission catalog (the full set, or an "Administrator" role with all permissions) + the first admin User (email + argon2-hashed password) assigned that role — so the new tenant can immediately log in.
   - apply the chosen industry template (industry.loader.apply_template) → COA, UoMs, tax codes, currencies, custom fields, terminology, numbering, module toggles all instantiated.
   - optionally instantiate a little demo data? The spec says "demo data instantiated automatically" — but full demo data is Phase 16 (seed.py). For 14.2, the onboarding instantiates the TEMPLATE config (COA/units/tax/numbering/workflows) automatically; "demo data" (transactions) is Phase 16's seed. DECIDE: onboarding does the config instantiation (via the template) + creates the admin user; transactional demo data is out (Phase 16). Document. (If trivial to seed a couple of master records, optional; prefer config-only.)
   - return the created tenant + admin user summary (NOT the password) + what was instantiated (counts: N accounts, N UoMs, etc.).
3. schemas: OnboardTenantRequest {company_name, slug?, industry_template, admin_email, admin_password, currency?}, OnboardTenantResponse {tenant_id, slug, admin_user_id, template_applied, instantiated_summary {accounts, uoms, tax_codes, ...}}.
4. router: POST /api/v1/onboarding/tenants (system-admin guarded; idempotent by slug) + GET /api/v1/onboarding/templates (proxy/convenience to list available industry templates for the wizard's picker — or reuse the industry endpoint; thin). Mount.
5. The whole onboarding is ONE transaction: tenant + role + user + template apply commit together or roll back. A bad template name or duplicate slug fails cleanly before partial creation.
6. docs/modules/admin.md (or industry.md, wherever onboarding lives): the onboarding flow (company → template → instantiated config + admin user), the auth model (system-admin guarded), idempotency, what's instantiated vs Phase-16 demo data. DECISIONS.md D-061 (onboarding orchestration: where it lives + why (§5-legal import direction), the tenant+admin-user+role+template-apply single transaction, the system-admin auth model, config-instantiation-not-transactional-demo).
7. Tests: test_onboarding.py (onboard a tenant with a template → tenant + admin role (with permissions) + admin user created, the template instantiated (COA accounts exist, UoMs exist, terminology set, numbering configured — assert via the respective queries under the new tenant's context), the admin user can authenticate (login works), idempotent (duplicate slug → 409), bad template → clean failure no partial tenant, the whole thing one transaction), test_onboarding_api.py (the endpoint, the system-admin guard (a non-system caller is rejected), the templates-list convenience, the response summary). HEED #53.

RULES: no TODO/stub/dead-file; absolute imports; ruff + pytest FULLY green SQLite (`-m "not pg and not perf"`) AND `-m pg` (reset pg schema, alembic upgrade head, run -m pg); delete stray atlas.db; every file <400 lines; comments only non-obvious; don't print file contents. Update PROGRESS.md + tick PLAN 14.2 + DECISIONS.md D-061. If NO migration needed, say so. Run STRUCTURE §9 self-check (esp. §5 — confirm the onboarding orchestrator's import direction creates no cycle) and report it.

Return: files created/changed, where onboarding lives + WHY (the §5-legal import direction, what 14.1's loader actually imports), the onboard_tenant flow (tenant+role+user+template in one transaction), the system-admin auth model, what's instantiated vs Phase-16 demo, whether a migration was needed, test counts (SQLite total+new, pg), §9 self-check, deviations.

1	"""Industry template loader (PLAN 14.1 / D-060): read + validate + idempotently apply a template.
2	
3	The headline differentiator (Atlas's answer to SAP industry solutions): a tenant picks one of the
4	five shipped templates at onboarding and this loader instantiates its whole configuration —
5	COA preset, tax codes, currencies, UoMs, item categories, typed custom fields, approval presets,
6	module toggles, terminology overrides and numbering formats — in ONE transaction.
7	
8	Two entry points:
9	
10	* ``load_template(name)`` — read ``industry-templates/{name}.yaml``, validate the raw dict against
11	  ``industry-templates/_schema.yaml`` (the declarative single source of truth, D-060), then parse
12	  it into a typed :class:`IndustryTemplate`. Pure + side-effect-free; cached per process (the files
13	  are shipped, immutable at runtime). The router and the tests call it directly.
14	
15	* ``apply_template(session, tenant_id, name)`` — the idempotent provisioning path. Runs under
16	  ``system_context`` (provisioning, D-007) inside the caller's ``run_in_uow`` (D-011). It:
17	    1. resolves the existing :class:`TenantIndustryConfig` — if the SAME template is already
18	       applied it is a NO-OP (returns the row); a DIFFERENT one raises ConflictError (a tenant's
19	       industry is chosen once, D-060);
20	    2. records the config row;
21	    3. applies the CORE/ADMIN-owned slices DIRECTLY (industry may import core + admin): custom-field
22	       defs (core/custom_fields, idempotent get-or-create), numbering sequences (core/numbering,
23	       idempotent ensure), terminology + module-toggle TenantSettings (admin table, upserted);
24	    4. PUBLISHES :class:`IndustryTemplateApplying` carrying the validated template — finance,
25	       inventory and procurement each create THEIR slice idempotently in the same transaction via
26	       their provisioning handlers (the §5-clean seam: industry NEVER imports their services).
27	
28	The whole apply is one unit of work: any handler failure rolls the WHOLE thing back (D-011), so a
29	half-applied template can never persist.
30	"""
31	
32	import functools
33	import uuid
34	from pathlib import Path
35	from typing import Any
36	
37	import yaml
38	from sqlalchemy import select
39	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
40	
41	from app.core.custom_fields import ensure_field_def
42	from app.core.events import publish
43	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError
44	from app.core.models import JSON_VARIANT  # noqa: F401 - documents the TenantSetting value type
45	from app.core.numbering import ensure_sequence
46	from app.core.tenancy import system_context
47	from app.modules.admin.models import TenantSetting
48	from app.modules.industry.constants import (
49	    MODULE_TOGGLES_SETTING_KEY,
50	    SHIPPED_TEMPLATES,
51	    TERMINOLOGY_SETTING_KEY,
52	)
53	from app.modules.industry.events import IndustryTemplateApplying
54	from app.modules.industry.schema_validator import IndustrySchemaError, validate_against_schema
55	from app.modules.industry.schemas import IndustryTemplate
56	
57	# industry-templates/ is a TOP-LEVEL repo dir (STRUCTURE §1), four parents up from this file
58	# (industry -> modules -> app -> backend -> repo-root).
59	TEMPLATES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "industry-templates"
60	SCHEMA_PATH = TEMPLATES_DIR / "_schema.yaml"
61	
62	
63	@functools.cache
64	def _load_schema() -> dict[str, Any]:
65	    """The parsed _schema.yaml (the JSON-Schema). Cached: it is a shipped file, immutable at
66	    runtime."""
67	    return yaml.safe_load(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
68	
69	
70	@functools.cache
71	def load_template(name: str) -> IndustryTemplate:
72	    """Read, schema-validate and parse the shipped template ``name`` (D-060).
73	
74	    Raises NotFoundError (404) if ``name`` is not a shipped template, IndustrySchemaError (422) if
75	    the YAML violates _schema.yaml, and a Pydantic ValidationError if the typed parse fails (a
76	    build error — caught by test_templates_valid). Cached per process; the files are immutable at
77	    runtime."""
78	    if name not in SHIPPED_TEMPLATES:
79	        raise NotFoundError(
80	            message=f"Unknown industry template {name!r}",
81	            code="industry.template_not_found",
82	            details={"name": name, "shipped": list(SHIPPED_TEMPLATES)},
83	        )
84	    raw = yaml.safe_load((TEMPLATES_DIR / f"{name}.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
85	    validate_against_schema(raw, _load_schema())
86	    if raw.get("name") != name:
87	        # The schema enum permits any shipped name; this enforces file-stem == declared name so a
88	        # mis-named file (a copy-paste hazard) is caught, not silently applied as the wrong one.
89	        raise IndustrySchemaError(
90	            "/name", f"declared name {raw.get('name')!r} != file stem {name!r}"
91	        )
92	    return IndustryTemplate.model_validate(raw)

95	async def get_applied_config(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID):
96	    """The tenant's TenantIndustryConfig row, or None. The loader's idempotency anchor; also
97	    re-exported via queries for the UI."""
98	    # Local import: models import is module-internal; keeping it here avoids a top-level cycle with
99	    # the events module which imports schemas (no cycle in practice, but this keeps loader's
100	    # top-level imports to core/admin only, documenting the §5 boundary).
101	    from app.modules.industry.models import TenantIndustryConfig
102	
103	    with system_context():
104	        stmt = select(TenantIndustryConfig).where(
105	            TenantIndustryConfig.tenant_id == tenant_id
106	        )
107	        return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
108

110	async def _upsert_setting(
111	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, key: str, value: Any
112	) -> None:
113	    """Idempotent upsert of one admin TenantSetting under system_context. The terminology overrides
114	    and module toggles are admin-owned settings the loader writes directly (D-060: the simplest
115	    §5-clean option — admin owns Tenant/TenantSetting and industry may import admin models). Mutates
116	    an existing row so re-apply updates in place (and audit captures the diff)."""
117	    with system_context():
118	        existing = (
119	            await session.execute(
120	                select(TenantSetting).where(
121	                    TenantSetting.tenant_id == tenant_id, TenantSetting.key == key
122	                )
123	            )
124	        ).scalar_one_or_none()
125	        if existing is not None:
126	            existing.value = value
127	        else:
128	            session.add(TenantSetting(tenant_id=tenant_id, key=key, value=value))
129	        await session.flush()
130	
131	
132	async def _apply_core_slices(
133	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, template: IndustryTemplate
134	) -> None:
135	    """Apply the CORE/ADMIN-owned slices the loader owns directly (D-060): custom-field defs,
136	    numbering sequences, terminology + module-toggle settings. All idempotent (get-or-create /
137	    upsert) so re-applying the same template never duplicates. Each slice runs under
138	    ``system_context`` (provisioning) — the defs/sequences/settings are tenant-scoped reads+writes
139	    that stamp tenant_id explicitly (D-007)."""
140	    with system_context():
141	        for field in template.custom_fields:
142	            await ensure_field_def(
143	                session,
144	                tenant_id,
145	                entity_key=field.entity_key,
146	                field_key=field.field_key,
147	                label=field.label,
148	                data_type=field.type,
149	                is_required=field.required,
150	                default_value=field.default,
151	            )
152	        for sequence_name, fmt in template.numbering_formats.items():
153	            await ensure_sequence(
154	                session,
155	                tenant_id,
156	                sequence_name,
157	                fmt.prefix,
158	                fmt.padding,
159	                fmt.year_reset,
160	            )
161	    await _upsert_setting(session, tenant_id, TERMINOLOGY_SETTING_KEY, dict(template.terminology))
162	    await _upsert_setting(session, tenant_id, MODULE_TOGGLES_SETTING_KEY, dict(template.modules))
163	
164	
165	async def apply_template(
166	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, name: str
167	) -> "object":
168	    """Idempotently apply industry template ``name`` to ``tenant_id`` (D-060).
169	
170	    Call inside ``run_in_uow`` (the router/onboarding do): this records the config + applies the
171	    core/admin slices + publishes IndustryTemplateApplying; the finance/inventory/procurement
172	    handlers create their slices when run_in_uow drains the event before commit, so the whole apply
173	    is ONE transaction.
174	
175	    Idempotency: re-applying the SAME template is a no-op (returns the existing config unchanged —
176	    the core slices' get-or-create + the handlers' skip-if-exists make the second pass harmless);
177	    applying a DIFFERENT template raises ConflictError (a tenant's industry is chosen once, D-060).
178	    Returns the TenantIndustryConfig row."""
179	    from app.modules.industry.models import TenantIndustryConfig
180	
181	    template = load_template(name)
182	    existing = await get_applied_config(session, tenant_id)
183	    if existing is not None and existing.template_name != name:
184	        raise ConflictError(
185	            message=(
186	                f"Tenant already has industry template {existing.template_name!r}; "
187	                f"cannot switch to {name!r}"
188	            ),
189	            code="industry.template_conflict",
190	            details={"current": existing.template_name, "requested": name},
191	        )
192	    if existing is None:
193	        with system_context():
194	            config = TenantIndustryConfig(tenant_id=tenant_id, template_name=name)
195	            session.add(config)
196	            await session.flush()
197	    else:
198	        config = existing
199	
200	    await _apply_core_slices(session, tenant_id, template)
201	    publish(session, IndustryTemplateApplying(tenant_id=tenant_id, template=template))
202	    return config

94	async def create_role(
95	    session: AsyncSession,
96	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
97	    name: str,
98	    permission_keys: Iterable[str],
99	    *,
100	    is_system: bool = False,
101	) -> Role:
102	    """Create a tenant role and grant it the named permissions (D-009). Keys are
103	    validated against the GLOBAL catalog rows (core_permissions): a key that no code
104	    declares — and so was never synced — raises ValidationFailedError, enforcing 'tenants
105	    cannot invent keys nothing enforces'. Runs under system_context so the global
106	    core_permissions lookup is unfiltered while tenant_id is stamped explicitly."""
107	    keys = list(dict.fromkeys(permission_keys))
108	    role = Role(tenant_id=tenant_id, name=name, description=None, is_system=is_system)
109	    with system_context():
110	        rows = (
111	            await session.execute(select(Permission).where(Permission.key.in_(keys)))
112	        ).scalars().all()
113	        found = {permission.key: permission.id for permission in rows}
114	        missing = [key for key in keys if key not in found]
115	        if missing:
116	            raise ValidationFailedError(
117	                code="rbac.unknown_permission",
118	                message="Unknown permission key(s)",
119	                details={"keys": missing},
120	            )
121	        session.add(role)
122	        await session.flush()  # role.id needed for the grants below
123	        for key in keys:
124	            session.add(
125	                RolePermission(
126	                    tenant_id=tenant_id, role_id=role.id, permission_id=found[key]
127	                )
128	            )
129	        await session.flush()
130	    return role

136	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    role_id: uuid.UUID,
138	    token_version: int,
139	) -> UserRole:

141	    appear on the next request (D-009). token_version is passed so the exact cache key is
142	    invalidated. Runs under system_context for explicit tenant stamping."""
143	    assignment = UserRole(tenant_id=tenant_id, user_id=user_id, role_id=role_id)
144	    with system_context():
145	        session.add(assignment)
146	        await session.flush()
147	    invalidate(tenant_id, user_id, token_version)
148	    return assignment

159	    (D-009): create (or reuse) the admin role with the four admin keys and assign it."""

164	            )
165	        ).scalar_one_or_none()

167	        session, tenant_id, role_name, _ADMIN_PERMISSION_KEYS, is_system=True
168	    )
169	    await assign_role(session, tenant_id, user_id, role.id, token_version)
170	    return role
